disease_label_per_paper: Streptococcus intermedius brain abscess with lung abscess and aortic valve endocarditis
presentation_summary: 40-year-old man had about 20 days of persistent cough, asthenia, intermittent fever, intense headache, and worsening back and lumbar pain partially responsive to paracetamol and NSAIDs.
At the first emergency department, vital signs were blood pressure 140/80 mmHg, heart rate 105/min, respiratory rate 17/min, oxygen saturation 97% on room air, temperature 38 C, and GCS 15.
He had no focal neurologic deficits or meningeal signs; thoracic exam was normal, heart tones were described as paraphonic, abdomen was non-tender, and no major lymph nodes were palpable.
Blood tests showed WBC 12.9 x10^9/L with neutrophils 77.7% and CRP 1.2 mg/dL; SARS-CoV-2 antigen was negative and blood cultures were negative.

Non-contrast cranial CT showed a 36 mm necrotic-colliquative left subcortical occipital lesion with perilesional edema; later brain MRI confirmed abscess nature and communication with the trigone of the left lateral ventricle.

Chest CT showed a 63 mm pleural-based left lower-lobe consolidative lesion with a 16 mm internal cavity; later abscess culture grew Streptococcus intermedius and TEE plus dental CT supported aortic valve endocarditis and dental source context.
He underwent left occipital craniotomy and abscess drainage, received targeted ceftriaxone followed by oral amoxicillin/clavulanate, and recovered without relapse at three months.
